newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends flat ahead of holidays.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends flat ahead of holidays.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market finished weakly on Wednesday with most players having left early for the May 1 holiday and an industry dinner in the Thai rubber centre of Hat Yai on Friday, dealers said.

"It's not really very active. Some of the deals you'll see on the screen were done yesterday and were just registered today. Many people have gone up to Hat Yai. They may as well go since nothing much is happening here," a trader said.
"It's been a difficult week. The big boys have already left for Thailand. Japan is practically out for Golden Week. People are in a holiday frame of mind," another trader said.
Traders said the ongoing Golden Week holiday season in Japan and the unresolved strike at Goodyear Tire also kept most people on the sidelines this week.
Dealers said the strike has knocked prices of SIR20 in Palembang down to around 46.00-46.50 U.S. cents a kg when it was hovering closer to 50 cents a few weeks ago.

At around 0945 GMT, June RSS3 was seen at 106.75 U.S. cents a kg from 107.25 cents. October/December RSS1 was seen at 157.50 Singapore cents (US$1.09) a kg from 158.50 cents. January/March TSR20 was seen at 105.75 U.S. cents a kg from 107.75 cents.
